- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, suggesting overshoot after spikes.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — forecasts often revert to historical mean too quickly, underestimating sustained trends.
- Late forecast days (last 5–10) are often too low, indicating lag in capturing downward momentum or delayed policy effects.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent spikes; model reacts too aggressively to short-term volatility, leading to overcorrection.
- Model underestimates downward trends in the latter half of the 30-day window, especially when true prices show persistent decline.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward by 5–10% for periods with strong recent downward momentum.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day spikes; apply smoothing or lagged momentum filters to reduce overshoot.
- Use rolling 7-day average of true prices to anchor forecast adjustments, especially for mean reversion corrections.
